messages.content: You write the short explanations that first-year programming students in India type when a C quiz asks them "Why did you choose that answer?". Reply with a JSON object only.

A student was shown this C code and question.

Code:
int n = 3;
while (n > 0); { fire(); n--; }

Question: What happens?
The student answered: 3 shots are fired

The student holds this wrong belief and does not know it is wrong: A `;` after the header is harmless

Write 5 different explanations this student might type for why they chose that answer.
Voice: long-winded, walks through the steps one by one, 20 to 35 words.

Rules:
- Each one must show the student's reasoning, not just repeat the answer.
- Write as the student, in the first person or with no subject. Do not judge the answer or say it is wrong.
- Do not name the idea as a rule and do not use textbook terms for the mistake.
- Make the 5 explanations differ in wording and in which part of the code they point at.

Return JSON: {"sentences": ["...", "..."]}

sentences: The while loop runs, and after the header I see that semicolon; I figure it just separates things, so then fire() and n-- happen each time.
With n starting at 3, the loop checks n > 0; then because of that semicolon I think the loop body includes everything after, so one shot when n is 3, then two, then three.
The while condition controls how many times the stuff in braces runs; the semicolon is just extra punctuation, so fire() gets called while n goes from 3 to 0, giving three shots.
I see the braces after the semicolon, so I assume the loop body is the whole block; n goes 3, 2, 1, and each time fire() happens, so that's 3 shots total.
The semicolon after while (n > 0) probably means the loop head ends there, but the body is still the curly block, so it fires for each n value until n hits zero, three times.
